the paper deals with the lexical item po in Korean.
this paper argues that there are three different ways in which the lexical item po can be used: (i) as a lexical verb 'to see' (ii) as a modal 'to try' (iii) as a circumstantial evidence marker.
The main takeaway from our work is that
po can be used as either an auxiliary or a lexical verb depending on the clause structure of the sentence in which it is used.

the three uses of po provide evidence for the presence of three distinct functional projections at the right periphery, which we label the Evidentiality Phrase (EvP), the Subjunctivity Phrase (SubjP), and the Epistemic Modality Phrase (EPMODP), respectively.
